source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's NVA9 campus in Sterling, Virginia publishes 38 MW of IT capacity and 700,000 square feet of technical space, and ranks 16th among the 29 Virginia facilities that publish a megawatt figure.

The pattern here is a facility with a large published power envelope and a large technical footprint, but no published rack count, accelerator count, or power density. That gap matters for AI because the same 38 MW supports roughly 950 racks at 40 kW per rack or roughly 3,800 racks at 10 kW per rack. The megawatt figure is the operator's, the rack count is an assumption, and the two should not be quoted as the same thing.

Virginia is the largest state on the map by a wide margin, with 376 mapped facilities and 2,563.4 MW of published capacity across the 29 that publish a figure. NVA9's 38 MW places it in the top tier of that published set. Because most mapped Virginia sites publish no megawatt figure at all, the 2,563.4 MW total is a floor rather than a full accounting of what the state has built.

The data does not say who occupies the campus, what workloads it hosts, or whether it holds any certifications. The certification field is empty, which means the spec page does not state whether the site is qualified for federal, financial, or health-data workloads. A reader should treat that as missing information rather than as a claim about what the campus can host.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
